newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher, but investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher, but investors sidelined.

text.p: Swiss shares ended higher after a quiet day with investors largely on the sidelines ahead of various U.S. economic data later in the week, dealers said.
Sentiment was generally good against the backdrop of a firming U.S. dollar and the favourable interest rate environment, one dealer said.

Tension in the market, however, was rising before Tuesday's U.S. employment cost index, which is considered to be an important indicator of U.S. inflation trends. Today's U.S. family homes sales did not influence the market much.
Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 21.0 points, or 0.44 percent, to 4,793.3 points, after touching 4,801.8.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended at 3,037.56 points, up 13.32 points, or 0.44 percent, from Friday's close.
Total bourse turnover reached 1.39 billion francs.

Actively-traded UBS bearer shares outperformed the market with an advance of 12 francs to 1,353. Dealers said this may be due to the fact that UBS has recently lagged behind somewhat. CS Group, which was in demand initially, ended flat at 163.75 francs.
Novartis registereds, which led the active list, added eight francs to 1,893. Roche certificates recovered from Friday's losses, climbing 65 francs to 12,175.

Swiss Re gave up earlier gains to close six francs lower at 1,650. The company said in a statement after bourse close that it planned to set up a new division for its Alternative Risk Transfer Market (ART) activities.
ABB, Electrowatt, Holderbank and Surveillance also posted losses among blue-chips.
Registered shares of watchmaker SMH jumped two francs to 192.50. CEO Nicolas Hayek said in a Reuters interview he expected an increase in 1997 sales and profits from 1996.
